Commentary.Commentary: Now Pakistan will really need their batters to step up here. The wicket is turning and New Zealand will hope to gain a first innings lead. Remember, Pakistan will be batting last in this game, so any sort of a lead will be very handy. Stay tuned.

The Pakistan bowling began brilliantly as Yasir Shah ran through the top order. However, as Day 1 progressed the Pakistan bowling lost some steam. Towards the end though they came back strongly but let New Zealand off the hook today morning. Asif was the star with a fifer while after doing the initial damage, Yasir Shah kept it tight from one end. Their pacers weren't much effective for most parts.

A commendable effort in the end by New Zealand. Not many would have thought they would get to the total they have especially when they were reeling at 72-4. However, their skipper stepped up, he along with Watling first stitched in a 104-run stand. Williamson perished 11 short of a ton but Watling continued with the tail and helped New Zealand to put a competitive total on the board.

The day started with BJ Watling and Somerville frustrating the Pakistanis. The latter blocked everything that came his way and the former was the one who did the job of scoring. The wicket-keeper got to his half ton and revived hopes of New Zealand getting to the 300-run mark. Bilal Asif though had different ideas as he ran through the tail. Pakistan though would feel they took longer than they would have liked to wrap the innings up.

Bilal Asif walks off to a standing ovation and he deserves every bit of it. There were questions raised about his performances before the game but he has silenced the critics in style. Picks all the three wickets which had to be taken today and ends with a fifer. However, New Zealand have added 45 handy runs and they will surely be happy with where they are placed in the game.

Danny Morrison interviewing Watling, the latter starts by saying he is very happy with the way he is playing. Also mentions there are a few cracks in the wicket and it will deteriorate even more. He also adds that he enjoys batting but it was tough to find gaps.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the third Test between Pakistan and New Zealand. The hosts finished Day 1 on top and they would be looking to wrap up the remaining three wickets quickly. On the other hand, the Kiwis would like to add as many runs as possible. With the wicket already turning something around 260-270 would be a competitive total. Stay tuned to find out how it unfolds on Day 2.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Pakistan would like to wrap up the last three wickets quickly on Day 2. While the Kiwis, would like to be somewhere around the 300-run mark. Should be an interesting day of cricket. The action resumes on Tuesday at 1000 local (0600 GMT). ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

Earlier in the day, the debutant, Shaheen Afridi started off brilliantly taking the wicket of Tom Latham. But Jeet Raval and Kane Williamson did manage to form a partnership of some sort. Yasir Shah though then came to the fore and ran through the middle order just before Lunch. Post that, a partnership of 104 between Kane Williamson and BJ Watling took the Kiwis to safer shores but quick wickets in the end sees Pakistan walk off as the happier side.

This session - 84 runs and 3 wickets. Pakistan's session and Pakistan's day one can say. They not only managed to break the 104-run stand between Williamson and Watling but have also picked up two more. When Watling and Williamson were batting, the Kiwis would have aimed for something around 300 but the spinners, along with Hasan Ali have now given Pakistan a chance to restrict New Zealand under 250.

Pakistan on the other, will need to break this partnership quickly. One would believe it is just the matter of one wicket and the hosts will then have a go at the fragile lower-order of New Zealand. Appeal for an LBW has been turned down. Sarfraz has gone for the review. Looks close. Latham is the man in question.

OUT! Three reds and Latham has been given his marching orders. Shaheen Afridi gets his maiden Test wicket and boy, it means a lot to him. The way he is celebrating it, just shows how happy he is. Once again it is the in-dipper. He lands it on a length around off, Latham looks to defend but the ball jags back in sharply. He misses and the ball hits his pads. The bowler appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Pakistan go for the review. Replays roll in and they show the on-field call has to be overturned. An excellent review from Pakistan. Ideal start for them as they have struck early.

Ross Taylor who is up for an interview, starts by saying we were completely outplayed in the last game. He also says it is tough playing in Asian conditions. Also mentions Pakistan are a good and competitive side. He is looking forward to play well in this Test.

With the batters in good form and bowling coming to the party, Sarfraz would want the same and win the Test series. Coming to the visitors, Williamson would like his team to come back stronger and would want to win this series.
